prompt: Count how many declared methods of a class carry a custom runtime annotation using reflection. Complete the countMarked method in the starter file; the @Marked annotation and sample classes above it are the test subjects.
explanation: Annotations are metadata attached to code; only annotations declared with @Retention(RetentionPolicy.RUNTIME) survive into the running JVM where reflection can query them. Method.isAnnotationPresent(Marked.class) asks each declared method whether it carries the annotation, so counting is a loop with an if. This inspect-and-count pattern is exactly how frameworks like JUnit find @Test methods.
hints: Loop over c.getDeclaredMethods() just like listing methods.
m.isAnnotationPresent(Marked.class) returns true when the method is annotated.
Only RUNTIME-retained annotations are visible here -- that is why @Marked declares its @Retention.
